title: The House That Learned to Build Itself

features.name: the-shed-that-adds-itself
features.desc-on-touch: You touch the corrugated wall and feel it warm from yesterday's sun. The shed breathes—each intake-breath a new plank appearing, each exhale a re-mortaring. It is building itself from a memory of shelter it has not yet finished having.

features.name: the-nail-dreaming-straight
features.desc-on-touch: A nail driven through timber, holding something that wasn't there when it entered. The wood grain has rewoven itself around the metal—an argument that ended as accommodation.

features.name: the-eaves-that-remember-rain
features.desc-on-touch: The gutter-edge traces shapes of water that has not yet come, stains showing seven future storms. The house learns weather from its own reflection in still air.

features.name: the-window-that-sees-inward
features.desc-on-touch: Looking through, you see the space the house contains and the space it is contained by at once. The pane is perfectly clear and perfectly obscured.

features.name: the-threshold-with-all-footprints
features.desc-on-touch: The doorstep is still wet from being laid. It shows your footprint and the footprints of everyone this house will shelter, all arriving at once from every future.

features.name: the-frame-that-waits
features.desc-on-touch: An empty frame on the eastern wall. What waits inside it is exactly what you are about to remember having lost. The house offers to remember for you.

inscription: it built itself up one thought at a time, each board a decision to stay

file.name: ShedLog_Incremental_Construction.txt
file.note: Nails placed, each entry describing itself as it was written. Later entries describe the wood before it arrived. The final entry describes the beginning of the final entry.

reverie.title: REVERIE — the shed-raising that was also a goodbye
narr: She held the timber level while you measured. The frame
was only half-built when she asked if houses dream of the
people who build them, or if people dream first and the
building just learns to follow. You didn't answer. The light
was failing. You nailed on until you could barely see, and
she held each board in place like it was something alive.

exits.label: deeper into rooms where walls choose their own thickness
toward the framework that has learned the language of its own wood
